title: Bitwise OR of Adjacent Elements
statement: Combine every two neighbouring values of `nums` with the bitwise OR operator and return the results, in order, as a new array. The result is one entry shorter than `nums`: its entry at index `i` is `nums[i] | nums[i + 1]`.
notes:
## Intuition

Each output value depends only on two neighbours, so there is nothing to search or remember: walk over every adjacent pair once and combine them with the bitwise OR operator. A bit is set in `a | b` exactly when it is set in `a`, in `b`, or in both, so the result is never smaller than either input. Done by hand, you would write both numbers in binary and keep each digit position that is 1 in at least one of them; the `|` operator does every position at once.

## Approach

1. Let `n` be the length of `nums` and create `answer` with `n - 1` slots.
2. For every index `i` from `0` to `n - 2`, read `left = nums[i]` and `right = nums[i + 1]`.
3. Store `left | right` in `answer[i]`.
4. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 3, 7, 15]`, so `answer` has 3 slots.

- `i = 0`: `1 | 3` is `01 | 11 = 11`, which is `3`.
- `i = 1`: `3 | 7` is `011 | 111 = 111`, which is `7`.
- `i = 2`: `7 | 15` is `0111 | 1111 = 1111`, which is `15`.

The result is `[3, 7, 15]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one OR per adjacent pair.
- Space: O(n) for the returned array (O(1) extra besides it).

## Pitfalls

- The answer has `n - 1` entries, not `n`; looping up to `n - 1` inclusive would read past the end.
- Use bitwise `|`, not logical `||`: `3 || 7` is `3`, while `3 | 7` is `7`.
- OR is not addition: `5 | 4` is `5`, because the shared bit `4` is counted once.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `answer` | the result, one value per adjacent pair |
| `i` | index of the left element of the current pair |
| `left`, `right` | the two neighbouring values being combined |

narration.2: Remember how many values there are.
narration.3: There is one output value per adjacent pair, so the result has n - 1 slots.
narration.4: Visit every pair (i, i + 1); the last pair starts at index n - 2.
narration.5: Take the left value of the pair.
narration.7: Bitwise OR keeps every bit that is set in either value.
narration.9: Every pair has been combined; return the result.
